question.problem: The $9$th and $10$th terms of an arithmetic sequence are $49$ and $45,$ respectively. Determine the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence.
question.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term is given by 

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d,
$$

so we need to figure out the first term ${a}_{1}$ and the common difference $d.$ 

Since the terms ${a}_{9}=49$ and ${a}_{10}=45$ are consecutive, we can subtract them to find the common difference:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{10}-{a}_{9} \\  & =45-49 \\  & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use one of our known values, say, ${a}_{9}=49,$ to determine the first term of the sequence. Since ${a}_{9}$ is $8$ jumps after ${a}_{1},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{9} & ={a}_{1}+8d \\ 49 & ={a}_{1}+8(-4) \\ 49 & ={a}_{1}-32 \\ 49+32 & ={a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =81.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the formula for the $n$th term of this arithmetic sequence is

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =81+(n-1)(-4) \\  & =81-4n+4 \\  & =85-4n.\end{aligned}
$$
